A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReflAct, with matching methods and core experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and Jericho, including baseline comparisons, ablations, enhancement-module experiments and behavioral analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Qwen3-8B and BabyAI evaluations, prompt sensitivity experiments, reasoning-step comparisons and task-specific failure analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same goal-state reflection followed by action generation and the same one-shot prompting approach. The expanded environment-specific instructions document implementation details without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds BabyAI, extending evaluation to five tasks involving navigation and object interactions in a 2D grid world. The existing ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and Jericho coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding existing experiments retain NoThinking, ReAct, Plan-and-Act, Reflexion, WKM, RAFA and MPO. Qwen3 is an additional agent backbone. Newly discussed SwiftSage and KnowSelf are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New evaluations use Qwen3-8B with thinking mode disabled and BabyAI with 10 episodes per task, 50 episodes total, a 128-step limit and average progression. Appendix I adds controlled prompt variants and an average reasoning-step metric. Existing benchmark splits and success criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds instruction and ICL-example paraphrasing tests, reasoning-step comparisons, ALFWorld task-level success breakdowns and diagnoses of Heat/Clean failures. Figure 26 adds a book-and-desklamp case. These substantially extend the retained ablation, hallucination and behavioral analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. New results remain point estimates; BabyAI episode counts describe evaluation sample size rather than an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original main results are retained, while Tables 3–8 add model, benchmark, prompt-variant, reasoning-step and task-specific results. For example, Qwen3 ALFWorld success is 65.7 for ReAct versus 80.6 for ReflAct, and BabyAI GPT-4o progression is 64.0 versus 76.0. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the interaction history to end with the thought and action at t−1, instead of including the current outputs at t. This removes circular conditioning from the formal definition. The remaining mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution and claims about goal-state reflection, grounding and advantages over existing reasoning frameworks. The headline 27.7% average improvement and 93.3% ALFWorld success rate are unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussion identifies exploration limits and misunderstood environment rules as ReflAct failure mechanisms, explains output-format problems with Qwen3 thinking mode, and interprets prompt sensitivity and shorter trajectories. This materially expands the account of effectiveness and failure conditions, while retaining the original domain and token-cost limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices D.3 and K supply exact ablation prompts, full environment instructions, action lists, output formats and additional ALFWorld examples. BabyAI implementation information is also added. Hardware disclosures are unchanged. v2 removes the promised post-publication code release without supplying a ReflAct repository link.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds an imitation-learning comparison with ETO, SwiftSage and KnowSelf, emphasizing ReflAct's lack of parameter updates. References for SwiftSage, KnowSelf, Qwen3, BabyAI and BALROG are added. The broader positioning against reasoning backbones and enhancement modules remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized copyediting, acknowledgements and revised related-work prose accompany clearer setup and prompt subsections. The appendices gain sections and separate instructions from ICL examples, but the main narrative and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds six result tables, full instruction panels, additional prompt examples and an ALFWorld case-study figure. Existing appendix displays are relocated, and prompt panels gain titles and sometimes span pages. This substantially expands the visual presentation while preserving the original core figures and tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the assessability of this prompt-based method: missing ablation and environment instructions are supplied, prompt sensitivity is tested, and success-oriented examples are complemented by concrete ReflAct failure diagnoses. Qwen3 and BabyAI broaden empirical support while preserving the original results. These gains outweigh the removed code-release pledge, although absent uncertainty reporting and restricted added settings, including disabled Qwen3 thinking mode, still limit the conclusions.
